bodies.nativeSurface: Own-body NASA3D mosaic preserved; unchanged native Hera AFC2025 monochrome projected context and HiRISE2009 enhanced-colour resolved context. Exact mosaic coverage/frame/photometric transfer and shape/albedo registration remain unaudited.
measured: Deimos is a small irregular, heavily cratered moon with a smoother appearance from partly filled craters; NASA describes dark dusty surface material, not measured metre-scale grain placement.
Existing catalogue radius6.2km and orbital semimajor axis23457km preserved. Hera AFC acquired visible monochrome context2025-03-12, released2025-03-13.
modelled: Representative Sun at1.524AU uses skyGeometry, nominal90degree horizontal FOV; Sun outside frame.
Spherical Mars guide16.653984degrees at assumed observer distance23457−6.2km uses skyGeometry with3396.2km radius. This is not dated orbital alignment.

Wargnier et al.2025 HRSC/SRC photometry uses Hapke modelling of2004–2024 images. Reported darkness/porous dust interpretation is model dependent, not a calibrated transfer used in these illustrations; full parameter/shape audit remains open.
assumed: Hypothetical airless locality with dark gray fine regolith, shallow smooth slopes and sparse stones. Dust colour, grain sizes, fragments and slopes invented; no copied Moon/Mars/Phobos photograph or map.
Mars-facing observer with invented Mars pattern, phase/orientation and lighting. Exposure, field of view and reflected illumination artistic; no registered landing site or survivable landing claimed.
unknown: Exact surface composition, dust depth and local grain sizes are unknown; carbonaceous spectral analogy is not a measured compositional recipe.

Native globe longitude/frame, coverage gaps, radiometry and irregular shape registration require further audit. Hera monochrome exposure contrast and HiRISE enhanced channels do not establish calibrated naked-eye colour.
No live Deimos-specific scientific image stream verified. Hera2025 context is newer than HiRISE2009; no exhaustive newest-observation claim.

prompts.surface: Create one independent research-guided hypothetical local terrain illustration of DEIMOS, Mars's smaller airless moon. Wide 16:9, no text. Camera just above dark neutral gray dusty regolith, smooth rolling low-gravity crater slopes with shallow partially buried small depressions, a sparse scattering of small angular stones, much smoother than Phobos. No Phobos-style parallel grooves or ridges. Black vacuum sky above low irregular horizon. Directional sunlight upper left, pale gray dust highlights, near-black sharp shadows; artistic exposure raised to see dark material. Dust depth and grain sizes unknown, fragment placement and local geography invented. Not a photograph or registered landing site; do not copy, recolour or trace the Moon, Mars, Phobos or any observed surface map. No red soil, no atmosphere, blue sky, fog, vegetation, ice, water, buildings, spacecraft, people or glowing material. Sun outside the frame. Subtle granular texture and restrained physically dark appearance, no dense boulder field. This is an independent hypothetical terrain view, not an analog skin.
prompts.sky: Create one independent research-guided hypothetical SKY FROM DEIMOS, wide16:9 image with no text. Camera above very dark gray fine dusty regolith on Mars-facing hemisphere of small airless Deimos. Gentle smooth rolling crater slopes, sparse small stones, foreground lower quarter, no Phobos-style parallel grooves. Vacuum sky black. Mars centred horizontally in upper-middle sky, full round disc with slight gibbous shading, apparent diameter guide16.654degrees in nominal90degree horizontal camera; diameter must be14.64percent of image width (about245pixels on1672pixel canvas), considerably smaller than the planet in a Phobos sky. Mars must be a modest disc, not dominate the frame. Rust/ochre muted brown globe with independently invented soft broad variations and a very thin atmospheric rim only around Mars. No recognisable copied Mars geographic map or photograph; no observed Moon/Mars/Phobos skins, tracing or recolouring. Sun outside frame; no visible Sun. No fog, blue scattering, water, vegetation, dense starscape, spacecraft or humans. Foreground illumination soft gray direct sunlight, black shadows slightly filled by Mars; exposure and colour artistic. Hypothetical local terrain, Mars pattern, phase and orientation invented, no dated alignment or landing survivability claim. Smooth enough for compact preview. Keep Mars disc near14.64percent width.
